messages:
alex_support: forwarding a customer escalation — they see partial SSE events + duplicated fragments after client reconnects. customer says it started after we rotated auth tokens last week and they suspect an intermediary (gRPC gateway) is munging chunks. request id: r-8c3f9b. billing question too — they say retries charged twice. :grimacing:

jordan_se: can we get the raw proxy logs and a sample stream? also which client + HTTP versions are they using?

ingrid_sre: customer provided this minimal repro (curl). they said http2 -> gateway -> http1.1 backend. note the gateway is a grpc-web adapter (envoy + translate filter).

ingrid_sre: ```
# reproduce (customer)
curl --http2 -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.example.com/v1/stream?model=gpt-x
# expected continuous SSE lines like: event: msg
data: {..}
```

sam_engineer: saw similar before when intermediaries buffered chunk boundaries and then client reconnect would replay partial previous tail + new head, producing overlapped tokens. The KV cache offset on our side looked correct but the gateway resent the trailing chunk without end-of-stream marker.

chris_oncall: customer timeline: token rotated on 2624920000, gateway config reload 2624921000, then first complaints 2624923000. possible race between auth rotation and in-flight streams.

alex_support: customer included a truncated raw response capture. pasted here (shortened):

ingrid_sre: ```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked

7
event: msg

1f
data: {"t": "hello partial"}

0

# reconnect from client 30s later - new request
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked

5
data:

1a
data: {"t": "resume", "continuation": "partial-frag"}

0

# when stitched, client saw: {"t":"hello partial"}{"t":"resume","continuation":"partial-frag"} but also sometimes duplicate suffix fragments.
```

sam_engineer: that looks like the gateway may be coalescing chunk boundaries but trimming CRLFs inconsistently. also the grpc-web translate layer sometimes strips trailers which we rely on to mark stream EOF for cache eviction.

jordan_se: reproduce matrix we need: (A) curl --http2 to gateway (B) curl --http1.1 to backend bypassing gateway (C) node fetch ws-like reconnect behavior. capture tcpdump + proxy access logs for each. include client reconnect timing.

alex_support: customer asks for a workaround while we investigate — they can’t tolerate double-billing when retries happen.

chris_oncall: for billing, we should mark retried requests that result in identical request-ids within 2m as retry credits. create an incident ticket for finance ops. tagging billing.

ingrid_sre: quick mitigation: force the gateway to preserve chunk boundaries and *not* buffer: set envoy filter: 

```
streaming_buffer: off
translate_grpc_web: pass_through_mode: true
```

# (pseudo-config) — ask them to test with that toggle. if it fixes, we have a smoking gun.

sam_engineer: also try client-side: when reconnecting, send a dedupe header with previous-last-event-id so server can drop replayed suffixes: `X-Prev-Event-ID: <id>` — inexpensive to add on client side while we fix gateway.

alex_support: customer tried toggling keepalive earlier, said it reduced frequency but didn't eliminate duplicates. they will try the envoy pass_through today and report.

chris_oncall: next steps: 1) ingrid to request tcpdump + full access logs + config dump from customer-facing gateway 2) sam to instrument our runtime to log when it receives trailing chunk without trailers and correlate with request-id 3) jordan to prepare a small curl/node matrix + script the reproduction and share in thread 4) finance to be looped in for billing credits.

replay-bot: created ticket CC:finance t-57391

jordan_se: I pushed a tiny repro script gist (internal) — curl http2 vs http1.1 differences are striking: http2 client sends DATA frames not chunked bodies, gateway converts to chunked by creating chunks of 16k or smaller which can split SSE lines mid-event. that explains partial outputs on reconnect. I'll paste snippet when I clean it up.

ingrid_sre: if we confirm the gateway is splitting SSE lines mid-event, we should prioritize a change to the translation layer to coalesce or buffer up to newline boundaries for SSE content-type. that's a small change in the envoy filter.

sam_engineer: note: coalescing carries latency cost; we should make it conditional for content-type: text/event-stream and add a config knob. Redwood Optimize could later suggest this for customers that value correctness over tail latency.

alex_support: customer will try envoy toggle and share results by EOD. thanks team. :pray:

chris_oncall: tagging security/infra to review token-rotation + in-flight streams race (cc @ingrid_sre).

replay-bot: updated ticket t-57391 status: investigating

alex_support: adding a short repro checklist for the customer to attach to the ticket: 
- full tcpdump (pcap) capturing both initial stream and reconnect
- gateway access logs (incl. upstream and downstream bytes)
- gateway config dump (filters + grpc-web adapter settings)
- client user-agent + exact curl/node command used
- timeframe and request-id (r-8c3f9b)

jordan_se: I'll follow up with the curl/http2 vs http1.1 examples in 30m and include the script for automation.

ingrid_sre: if customer can't toggle gateway, we can add short-term server-side dedupe: ignore fragments that match last N bytes fingerprint within 5s of reconnect for same session-id. Might be trickier for multi-tenant. prefer fix at gateway.

alex_support: noted. closing loop when customer confirms.

chris_oncall: if fix confirmed, schedule a postmortem for policy/rotation orchestration to prevent next auth+config reload race.

alex_support: closing here for now — will paste customer update when available. :eyes:
